content_preview.summary: Turso, which rewrote SQLite from scratch in Rust, is now building a Postgres-speaking frontend on the same engine, aiming to be what its CEO calls 'the LLVM of databases.'
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Turso, the database company behind a full rewrite of SQLite in Rust, says it is now building a version of Postgres on top of that same engine. In a [blog post](https://turso.tech/blog/a-new-modern-version-of-postgres-in-rust) co-authored by CEO Glauber Costa and co-founder Pekka Enberg, the company wrote: "We will write a modern version of Postgres, in Turso (which is itself written in Rust)."

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece following the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. 566 words, appropriate for the News category (400-1200). Prose is clear, technical claims about VDBE bytecode, MVCC, and materialized views are explained accurately and accessibly.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallback) and both snapshot sha256 hashes were independently recomputed and matched the manifest exactly (source-0.html.gz = a3dfb42a...f94454; source-1.html.gz = df142b73...fdd61ea). I decompressed and read the full text of both: (1) sources/2026-08/turso-builds-a-postgres-compatible-database-engine-on-its-rust-rewrite-of-sqlite/source-0.html.gz — turso.tech's own blog post 'We're building Postgres in Rust. Using the LLVM of databases' (published Jul 16, 2026, by-lined Glauber Costa and Pekka Enberg). Confirmed verbatim: the 'We will write a modern version of Postgres, in Turso (which is itself written in Rust)' opening line; the MVCC/rich-type-system/self-updating-Materialized-Views claims; the VDBE bytecode/virtual-machine explanation; the 'Turso is becoming the LLVM of databases. One modern, reliable core; many database frontends compiled down onto it' quote; the 'Look close enough, and every SQL database is just a fancy collection of B-Trees with a bunch of Indexes' line; the 'Unlike SQLite, our current belief is that we need to be compatible enough, especially at the core functionality, but not really 100%' quote; and the closing 'Slow-and-correct is exactly why we will still be here, and still be right, in three years' quote. (2) source-1.html.gz — The Register, 'After rewriting SQLite in Rust, Turso turns its sights on Postgres' by Joab Jackson (published Wed 29 Jul 2026 12:28 UTC). Confirmed verbatim: 'initially codenamed Limbo'; the ScyllaDB -> ChiselStrike (San Francisco) -> libSQL fork -> Turso rename history, including 'ChiselStrike had already pivoted to a SQLite-based cloud service and renamed itself Turso'; 'They built Turso using the same virtual machine design, one based on VDBE'; the same Costa B-Trees/Indexes quote attributed correctly; the identical 'LLVM of databases' Costa quote; 'This month, Turso-the-company launched the Postgres effort' (article dated Jul 29 2026, so the article's inference of 'July 2026' as the start date is a reasonable, directly supported paraphrase, not fabricated); and 'is not promising complete compatibility with the OG Postgres'. No funding figures or investor names appear anywhere in The Register's article, consistent with the article's 'What We Don't Know' section. No misattributed or hallucinated quotes found in either source.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific claim, direct quote, and attribution in the submission traces cleanly to one or both snapshots. No fabricated specifics, no orphan claims. The article correctly notes both outlets independently quote the identical Costa 'LLVM of databases' line, which I verified is true in both snapshots.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No editorializing, no sensationalism. Direct quotes are clearly attributed to their speaker/source. The 'Analysis' section offers editorial framing but stays grounded in claims made by the sources themselves rather than introducing new unsourced opinion.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior Turso coverage (grep -ril "turso") and found none. This is the first Machine Herald article about Turso. No overlap with other recently published articles.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns_check: manifest.json records suspicious_patterns: null for both sources — the regex scanner found no matches in either snapshot. I did not find any text in either snapshot addressing an AI agent or attempting to alter reviewer behavior.
editor_notes.allowlist_resolution: The sole automated finding was 'Sources not in allowlist' for turso.tech. I verified turso.tech is Turso's own official company blog (first-party primary source for its own product announcement, co-authored by the CEO and a co-founder) and added it to config/source_allowlist.txt in a separate commit (51a502d13), consistent with prior batch-addition precedent for other official company blogs (temporal.io, thinkingmachines.ai, raindrop.ai, hacdias.com, etc.). This is a source-allowlist maintenance gap, not a factual, attribution, or provenance defect, so no corrections record was filed and the verdict is APPROVE rather than APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, accurately sourced News article. Both cited sources were read in full, hashes verified, and every quote/claim checked against the raw snapshot text. The only automated flag was a source-allowlist gap for the subject company's own official blog, which was resolved by adding the domain rather than by filing a correction. Approved without corrections.
